title: Tech Startup Battle
description: Lead your tech startup against a rival corporation. Deploy developers, designers, and marketers strategically to capture market share and outsmart the competition.
learning_objectives: Develop team management skills by coordinating specialized roles toward shared objectives
Practice strategic resource allocation by deploying limited talent across contested markets
Understand competitive strategy through head-to-head positioning against a corporate rival
Learn tech industry dynamics including funding cycles, talent acquisition, and patent wars
Build adaptive decision-making by responding to shifting competitive landscapes
Cultivate long-term planning by balancing product development against market expansion
how_to_play: Each turn you get 2 Action Points (AP). Moving a piece costs 1 AP, and using a special ability costs 1 AP.
CEO moves 2 squares in any direction. Developers move 1 square in any direction. Designers move 2 squares diagonally. Marketers move 2 squares in straight lines (N/S/E/W).
Capture enemy pieces by moving onto their square. Interns promote to Developer when reaching the last row.
Control resource tiles (Funding, Talent Pool, etc.) by placing your pieces on them. Each tile generates startup capital per turn.
Win by: capturing the enemy CEO, controlling 3+ resource tiles, or reaching $10M in startup capital.
Use each piece's unique abilities strategically — the CEO's Motivate ability and the Designer's creative pivots can turn the tide of any market battle.
objectives: Capture the rival Corp CEO for an instant market takeover victory
Control 3 or more key resource tiles for a market domination win
Build your startup capital to $10 million through strategic operations

storybook_pages.title: The Startup Arena
storybook_pages.text: Silicon Valley is booming and two rivals face off for market dominance. Your scrappy startup team of developers, designers, and marketers must outmaneuver a powerful corporate machine. Every sprint counts — the market is volatile and victory belongs to the most innovative team.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: two rival tech teams facing each other across a giant circuit board styled as a chess board, indigo and purple colors, glowing screens and code, startup office and corporate tower in background, digital illustration style

storybook_pages.title: Your Startup Team
storybook_pages.text:
CEO (King) — Your visionary leader, protect at all costs. Moves 2 squares any direction.
Developer (x3) — Core builders, move 1 square any direction.
Designer (x2) — Creative thinkers, move 2 squares diagonally.
Marketer (x2) — Growth hackers, move 2 squares in straight lines.
Intern (Pawn) — Eager talent, promotes to Developer at the far row!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: diverse tech startup team members as game pieces in a modern office, CEO at whiteboard as leader, developer with laptop, designer with tablet, marketer with megaphone, colorful modern illustration, game character design with tech theme

storybook_pages.title: The Market Battlefield
storybook_pages.text: The 8x8 board represents the competitive tech landscape with 5 key resource tiles: Funding rounds, Talent Pools, Market Share hotspots, Patent offices, and Tech Conferences. Control them to generate startup capital each turn and build your path to unicorn status!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: birds eye view of a colorful 8x8 game board with glowing tiles showing dollar signs, people icons, charts, documents, and conference halls, tech-themed with circuit patterns, digital game art with indigo color scheme

resource_narratives: Startup capital flows in from controlled market tiles — your runway extends!
Resource tiles generate revenue, fueling your startup's growth engine.
Market dominance pays dividends — startup capital collected from held positions.
tips: Protect your CEO at all costs — losing the founder means instant defeat.
Developers are your core strength. Use their versatility to control the center of the board.
Designers excel at unexpected diagonal attacks — use them to flank the corporate enemy.
Marketers dominate straight-line corridors. Position them to control resource tiles along rows and columns.
Push Interns forward aggressively — promoting one to Developer can swing the game.
Control at least 3 resource tiles for an economic victory without needing to capture the Corp CEO.
The CEO's Motivate ability is a game-changer — keep allies nearby to maximize its impact.
Watch for the AI's Managers — they mirror your Developers and can contest the center effectively.
Balance offense and defense: overextending leaves your CEO exposed to flanking attacks.
Funding tiles generate the most income. Prioritize capturing and holding them early.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.
